newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi's Mediaset stock rises in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi's Mediaset stock rises in Milan.

text.p: Shares in Mediaset, opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi's television and advertising group, rose strongly in active trade on the Milan bourse.

Traders said sentiment for the group was boosted by press reports of some form of accord in the upper house of parliament on reorganising legislation in the TV sector, and general signs of an easing of tension between the government and opposition.
"Every time there is less tension the share benefits," one trader said.
"There is no doubt that the wider political picture has a major impact on Mediaset's future," said Paola Toschi, analyst at Milla brokers.
At 1312 GMT, Mediaset was quoted 4.0 percent up at 7,590 lire after a high at 7,620 in volume of over 2.5 million shares.
The government wants to introduce wide-ranging legislation this summer for the TV sector which is dominated by Mediaset's three terrestrial channels and the state-owned RAI's three.
The Constitutional Court ruled three years ago that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three channels but changes have yet to be implemented.
"We think the group has good prospects and the uncertainty of regulations in the TV sector has weighed on the share price," she added.
Alberto Rolla of Pasfin said "We see a price target of 8,300 lire given the scenario that these uncertainties will likely be overcome."
